name: viewer
desc: Read your backlog on your phone, from a place you own
author: Amenbo

config.label: Where to carry
config.help: Whether this may carry to your Cloudflare Worker. It can only take the place away: ticking it still needs the Worker to exist before anything reaches it, and setup is what stands one up. Ticking nothing is an answer and it is honoured: the plugin stays enabled and carries nowhere.

config.label: Your Cloudflare Worker's URL
config.help: setup writes this when it stands the Worker up. There is nothing to type.

config.label: Token the Worker lets writes in with
config.help: setup generates this. There is nothing to type.

config.label: Key the records are encrypted with
config.help: setup generates this. There is nothing to type - the phone is given it by the QR, never over the network.

actions.label: 1. Get the app on your phone

agent.when: Setting up the phone viewer, pairing a phone with it, or carrying by hand what has not reached one yet

commands.does: Puts the App Store page for Amenbo Viewer on a QR the phone's camera reads, so the address does not have to be carried from this screen to the phone by hand. Asks nothing and keeps nothing
Opens Cloudflare's token screen in the browser, with the three permissions setup needs already ticked, and ends there. Asks nothing and keeps nothing — the token the page makes is pasted into setup
Stands up the Worker and its database in the user's own Cloudflare account, and generates the token and key. Takes a Cloudflare API token from the settings screen, a terminal or CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN
Carries by hand what has not reached the phone yet, encrypting a record at a time, over every route that is configured. The hook does this per write, so this is for what was left behind
Lists the phones that may read and when each was paired. Reads nothing over the network — the store compares hashes and does not answer what it holds
Cuts one phone off by the name it was paired under, at the store first and here after. The other phones carry on reading. Takes that name as its only argument
Pairs one phone: issues a read token, registers its hash, puts endpoint/token/key/name on a QR the camera reads, off the network. --label or the settings screen box names it; --terminal draws it here
Says where records are reaching right now — the places ticked under 'Where to carry' that also exist. Reads nothing over the network; the settings screen raises it, and a terminal may too
